jobs.description:
Job Posting: Air Pollution Specialist



State Air Resources Board


JC\-527508* 

Air Pollution Specialist
  

AIR POLLUTION SPECIALIST
$5,918\.00 \- $11,455\.00 per Month
  

New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.


**Final Filing Date:** **8/25/2026**


### **Job Description and Duties**


The California Air Resources Board (CARB) is seeking a motivated, innovative, and technically oriented individual to join our multidisciplinary team of scientists and engineers. This position plays a critical role in developing, maintaining, and enhancing CARB’s emissions inventories, which support State Implementation Plans (SIPs), community health initiatives, regulatory development, and air quality planning across California.  

The Emissions Inventory Section is responsible for maintaining and updating CARB’s statewide criteria pollutant and toxic air contaminant inventories. Staff work closely with California’s 35 air districts to collect stationary source emissions data required under state and federal regulations. The team also collaborates with CARB’s internal programs and local districts to gather emissions data for area wide, mobile source, and event categories. Using growth and control factors developed with district partners and CARB technical teams, the section forecasts emissions inventories to future years to support air quality modeling and planning.  

To improve data quality and accessibility, the section develops and maintains applications for emissions data collection, data management, and reporting. These tools provide communities, air districts, regulators, researchers, state agencies, and other stakeholders with reliable, transparent, and user friendly emissions data.  

This position serves a vital function in the section’s work by compiling and performing rigorous quality assurance on emissions inventories submitted by local air districts and internal CARB programs. The incumbent will collaborate closely with the team’s lead forecaster to develop control profiles informed by emerging regulations and new control technologies. In addition, the position will be responsible for creating analytical tools and summary reports to evaluate emissions inventory forecasts used for air quality modeling and planning. The incumbent will also prepare standardized documentation outlining internal procedures for updating emissions inventories and control profiles. Finally, the role involves working with CARB staff, other government agencies, and academic partners to apply advanced QA/QC methods and strengthen the overall accuracy and reliability of CARB’s emissions data.  

The work produced by this section is foundational to improving air quality statewide. In this position, you will directly support air quality planning, photochemical modeling, regulatory development, community level emission reduction strategies, and project level environmental assessments. Your contributions will help ensure the accuracy and reliability of emissions data used to guide California’s most important air quality and public health decisions.  

The ideal candidate will have a strong scientific and technical background in one or more of the following areas: emissions forecasting, air quality, air quality modeling, emissions inventory development, stationary source emissions, or a closely related field. Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, collaborative capabilities, and comfort working with large datasets are highly desirable.
You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


This position may be eligible for hybrid in\-office work and in\-state telework. The amount of telework is at the agency's discretion and is based on the California Air Resources Board’s (CARB) current telework policy. While the CARB may support telework, some in\-person attendance is also required.


The positions at the CARB may be eligible for telework with in\-person attendance based on the operational needs of the position under Government Code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria outlined in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program need. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of hybrid telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location at their own expense, as indicated on their duty statement.


Effective July 1, 2025, the California Department of Human Resources (CalHR) implemented the Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025\). PLP 2025 directs that each employee shall receive a 3 percent reduction in pay in exchange for 5 hours PLP 2025 leave credits, monthly. The salary range(s) included in the job advertisement do not reflect the 3 percent reduction in pay.


* Position located in a high\-rise building.
* Requires being stationary, consistent with office work, for extended periods.
* Standard office environment (artificial lighting, controlled temperature, etc.).
* Daily use of a personal computer, office equipment, and/or telephone.

jobs.description:
Job Posting: Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist)



Department of Food \& Agriculture


JC\-527396* 

Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist)
  

SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SPECIALIST)
$7,820\.00 \- $10,732\.00 per Month
  

New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.


**Final Filing Date:** **8/18/2026**


### **Job Description and Duties**


**Per CCR 249\.3, this job control may be used to fill subsequent vacancies.**  

**This is a 12\-month Limited Term (LT) position that may be extended up to 24 months or may become permanent.**  

Under the direction of the Environmental Program Manager I (Supervisory), the Senior Environmental Scientist Specialist (SES Spec) leads the coordination of activities of ERIHC from within the NS\&C Program. The SES (Spec) is the program lead, responsible for ensuring that the program commitments are met. The SES will provide technical coordination and training to CACs, administrative support staff, collaborating agencies, and other contractors related to the program’s commitments and objectives. The SES (Spec) must also establish effective working relationships and maintain cooperative liaison relationships with government agencies, agricultural industry, and the general public. This position is necessary to provide technical support to CACs and facilitate interagency coordination for addressing non\-compliant hemp cultivation activities.  

As an employee of the California Department of Food \& Agriculture (CDFA), you are required to perform the “essential functions” of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation. If you are interested in becoming part of a diverse and inclusive workforce where talent, experience, and expertise are valued, then CDFA is the place for you!!  

This CDFA work location is near restaurants, coffee shops, and a farmer’s market. We are within walking distance to light rail/public transportation, across the street from beautiful Capitol Park, and two miles from Downtown Commons (DOCO).  

This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. The CDFA does not participate in E\-Verify for employment authorization purposes.  

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


The duties of this job are performed indoors approximately ninety percent (90%) of the time in an office. The employee’s workstation is located inside an office building equipped with standard office equipment. The remainder of the time is spent traveling to meetings or district offices, outdoor locations, warehouses or facilities of industrial hemp production or sale. The employee may be exposed to extremes in temperature, dust, fumes, gases, and odors.  

  

Overnight and/or extended travel to various locations throughout the State may be required to accomplish work objectives in various environments. State vehicles are used to travel to these worksites. Rental vehicles and/or air travel may also be used.  

This position may/may not be eligible for telework. The amount of telework is at the discretion of the CDFA and based on the current telework policy. While the CDFA supports telework where possible, in\-person attendance may be required based on operational needs. Employees are expected to be able to report to their worksite with minimal notification if an urgent need arises, as determined by the Department.

### **Department Information**


The Mission of the California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA) is to safeguard a resilient food system and promote an equitable marketplace, cultivating a California grown food supply that is globally recognized for innovation, quality, and sustainability.  


  

As part of the Pest Exclusion Branch, the Nursery, Seed, and Cotton Program (NS\&C) is responsible for the enforcement of laws and regulations that ensure the quality and orderly marketing of nursery, seed, and cotton plant products. The mission of the program is to prevent the introduction and spread of agricultural pests and diseases in nursery and seed products, thereby protecting California’s environment, agricultural systems, and consumers against economic losses. The program coordinates statewide regulatory and inspection activities with county agricultural commissioners. In addition, the program maintains registration and certification services which provide the agricultural industry with clean planting stock.  

https://www.cdfa.ca.gov/plant/PE/nsc/

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
**Senior Environmental Scientist**

 **Senior Environmental Scientist**


**Brisbane or Cairns QLD**


RPS, A Tetra Tech company


RPS, A Tetra Tech company, is a global professional services firm delivering projects that define, shape and manage Australia's most important infrastructure, development and environmental initiatives.


With more than 5,000 professionals across 125 countries, we bring together technical excellence, practical thinking and a collaborative approach to solve complex challenges across infrastructure, energy, water, environment, urban development and resources.


Our Oceans \& Environment team partners with government and private sector clients to deliver innovative environmental solutions that support sustainable development while protecting our natural environment.


**The Opportunity**


Due to continued growth, we are looking for a Senior Environmental Scientist to join our Oceans \& Environment team in our Brisbane or Cairns offices.


This is an exciting opportunity to work on a diverse portfolio of infrastructure, renewable energy, transport, water and development projects across Queensland and Australia. You will collaborate with experienced environmental consultants and technical specialists to deliver environmental assessments, approvals and management solutions that help clients achieve successful project outcomes.


Whether you enjoy field work, technical reporting, environmental approvals or working closely with clients, this role offers excellent variety and the opportunity to grow your career within a supportive national team.


**What You Will Be Doing**


* Preparing environmental assessments, technical reports and environmental management plans.
* Assisting with environmental impact assessments and planning approval documentation.
* Conducting environmental investigations, literature reviews and data analysis.
* Supporting environmental approvals under Queensland and Commonwealth legislation.
* Coordinating inputs from technical specialists and project stakeholders.
* Working collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams.
* Building strong relationships with clients, regulators and internal stakeholders.
* Assisting with project planning, budgeting and delivery to meet client expectations.
* Supporting proposal preparation and business development activities.
* Ensuring work is delivered safely on time and to a high technical standard.


**About You**


You will be passionate about delivering practical environmental outcomes and enjoy working on a wide variety of projects in a collaborative consulting environment.


You will also bring:


* A degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Management or a related discipline.
* Experience working in environmental consulting, government or a related industry.
* Knowledge of Queensland environmental legislation and environmental assessment processes.
* An understanding of the Commonwealth Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999 (EPBC Act).
* Strong technical report writing and communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex information clearly.
* Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
* A collaborative approach and a commitment to delivering quality outcomes for clients.
* A current Australian driver's licence and willingness to undertake occasional field work and travel as required.


**Why Join RPS?**


At RPS, we believe our people are our greatest strength. We are committed to providing an inclusive and supportive workplace where you can develop your career while contributing to projects that create lasting value for our communities.


We offer:


* Professional development and career progression opportunities
* A supportive team culture that celebrates collaboration and success
* Flexible working arrangements to support work\-life balance
* Active wellbeing and community engagement initiatives
* Annual professional membership reimbursement
* Paid parental and partner leave
* $250 active lifestyle allowance per annum
* Additional annual leave purchase scheme and salary packaging options
* Professional and technical development programs, including study assistance, online learning and mentoring across portfolios
* Active office social events, Employee Assistance Program, service recognition and more


**Our Commitment**


At RPS, everyone is empowered to bring their best. We foster a workplace where different perspectives are valued, collaboration is encouraged and people are supported to grow professionally.


As part of Tetra Tech, we combine local knowledge with global expertise to deliver exceptional outcomes for our clients while creating opportunities for our people.


Ready to Make an Impact?


If you are looking to build your environmental consulting career with a respected global consultancy and work on projects that make a real difference across Queensland and beyond, we would love to hear from you.


Apply today and help shape a more sustainable future with RPS, A Tetra Tech company.

**Our Approach**


Our people live our purpose, deliver our promise, and demonstrate our behaviours every day. Our behaviours define who we are. Developed by our people, they underpin everything that we do. They create the memorable experiences we are known for and make RPS a great place to do great work.  

Stronger together is one of our five core behaviours and it is key to building a collaborative workplace. We encourage everyone to bring their best and to support others to do the same. By sharing knowledge, challenging each other to think differently, and fostering an environment of trust and respect, our people can learn, grow and thrive – and share in our success.

**Recruitment Agencies**


We have a Preferred Supplier List of trusted partners to assist us when required and do not acknowledge any speculative CVs or unsolicited candidate introductions from agencies not on this list. Please refer to the careers page
